items.title: Samoa leader apologises for Nazi salute after video from 2007 emerges
items.summary: Schmidt acknowledged that his actions "were inappropriate and capable of causing offence and hurt".
items.content:
Samoa's prime minister has apologised after a video emerged of him giving a Nazi salute while saying "Heil Hitler" at a family gathering.

In the seven-second clip filmed in July 2007, Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Schmidt is seen leading about a dozen people in the salute. "Raise your right hand, Heil Hitler!" he says, then thanks the group for responding.

Schmidt has acknowledged that his words and gesture "were inappropriate and capable of causing offence and hurt", adding that the clip was recorded at a private gathering and "not intended for the public".

"I reject Nazism, antisemitism, racism and all forms of political extremism," Schmidt said in a statement published on Facebook on Monday.

The footage was first reported by local outlet the Samoa Observer in a news story on Sunday.

It said the video was filmed at a Schmidt family reunion in July 2007, when Schmidt was deputy speaker of parliament and quoted a family member who said he was the master of ceremonies at the gathering.

Samoa, a tiny island nation of about 221,000 people, sits about halfway between New Zealand and Hawaii.

It was under Germany's control in the early 20th century, but the colonisation ended shortly after World War One broke out.

Schmidt, who has Samoan and German heritage, took office as the country's eighth prime minister in September 2025.

He wore a Jewish prayer shawl during his swearing-in ceremony and has made clear his support for Israel during the early days of his premiership, saying that Samoa "stood with Israel".

"If people around the world don't like it, that's up to them, but Samoa stands with the land of God... There is only one God our country believes in, the God of Israel," he had said.

items.title: Fort Hood shooter to be executed by firing squad - a first for US military since World War Two
items.summary: Nidal Malik Hasan killed 13 unarmed soldiers and injured another 32 in the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.
items.content:
The Pentagon has announced it will execute a former US Army major by firing squad, the first such military execution in more than 60 years.

Nidal Malik Hasan fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, injuring another 32.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell announced on social media on Monday that Secretary of War Pete Hegseth had made the recommendation and President Donald Trump approved it.

It will be the first military execution by firing squad since the end of World War Two.

Parnell said the secretary of the Army will set the time and place of the execution.

Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist from Virginia, killed 13 soldiers at the base in Texas in 2009 and later admitted in court he was the gunman and apologised for "any mistakes".

He said during his court-martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan.

The killings on 5 November 2009 were the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.

The attack took place in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines.

Hasan is currently one of four inmates on the US military's death row.

A military execution requires approval from the US president, according to military law.

It also requires appellate review and a final judgment on its legality to move forward.

The US Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces deemed the military death penalty unconstitutional in 1983 but it was reinstated the following year by an executive order under then-President Ronald Reagan.

Military executions differ from those carried out at the state level.

The majority of executions in the US are carried out on the state level, with 27 states, the military and the federal government still having capital punishment as a legally available option.

Death by firing squad is rather uncommon. There was an execution by firing squad carried out last year in South Carolina, a first for the state and the first time the method was used in the US in 15 years.

Four other states allow the use of a firing squad, including Idaho, Mississippi, Oklahoma and Utah.

Trump has been a proponent of the federal death penalty and re-instated it through an executive order on the first day of his administration in January 2025.

Under his predecessor, former President Joe Biden, the justice department had issued a moratorium on the federal use of the death penalty.

The executive order signed by Trump describes capital punishment as "an essential tool for deterring and punishing those who would commit the most heinous crimes and acts of lethal violence against American citizens".

items.title: Trump approva la fucilazione per l'autore della strage nella base di Fort Hood
items.summary: Nidal Hasan nel 2009 uccise 13 persone e ne ferì 32
items.content:
Donald Trump approva la fucilazione per Nidal Hasan, ex psichiatra dell'esercito condannato a morte nel 2009 per l'attacco nella base militare di Fort Hood nel quale ha ucciso 13 persone e ne ha ferite 32. Hasan è stato condannato negli anni scorsi da una giuria militare al termine di un processo di corte marziale in cui l'imputato aveva rinunciato a difendersi.

Il segretario alla Difesa Pete Hegseth "ha raccomandato, e Donald Trump ha approvato, la condanna a morte tramite fucilazione da parte di un plotone d'esecuzione dell'esercito statunitense per il terrorista condannato Hasan", che aveva urlato "Allah Akbar durante l'attacco. Il segretario alla Difesa deciderà l'ora e il posto dell'esecuzione. Il giorno del giudizio per Hasan è finalmente arrivato", ha detto il portavoce del Pentagono Sean Parnell.

Tutti i morti tranne uno erano soldati, tra cui una soldatessa incinta che si era buttata per terra implorando perché fosse risparmiato il figlio ancora non nato. La sparatoria finì solo quando Hasan fu colpito alla schiena da un militare che aveva reagito al fuoco. L'ex maggiore è rimasto paralizzato dalla vita in giù. L'ex psichiatra, musulmano di origini palestinesi, aveva detto di aver agito per proteggere ribelli islamici all'estero dall'aggressione degli Stati Uniti. Aveva ammesso di aver aperto il fuoco in un'affollata sala d'aspetto dove decine di soldati aspettavano l'ultima visita medica prima del dispiegamento al fronte in Iraq e Afghanistan.

items.title: Viaggio al centro della Terra: inizia in Valsesia
items.summary: Viaggio al centro della Terra: inizia in Valsesia
items.content:
Abbiamo fotografato gli anelli di Saturno, fatto atterrare rover su Marte e spedito sonde oltre i confini del sistema solare. Eppure il nostro pianeta resta in gran parte inesplorato proprio sotto i nostri piedi. Il pozzo più profondo mai scavato, quello della penisola di Kola, in Russia, si è fermato a circa 12 chilometri: appena lo 0,2% dei 6.371 chilometri che ci separano dal centro della Terra.
Per rendersi conto delle proporzioni, si può pensare a una mela. La crosta terrestre, con le sue montagne, gli oceani e le città, è sottile come la buccia. Sotto si estende il mantello, un enorme volume di roccia calda che scorre lentamente nell'arco di milioni di anni e che costituisce la parte più grande del pianeta.. Il Moho, la linea che nessuno ha mai toccato
Il confine tra crosta e mantello si chiama discontinuità di Mohorovičić, o più semplicemente Moho, dal nome del sismologo croato Andrija Mohorovičić che la individuò nel 1909. Studiando i terremoti nei Balcani, notò che a una certa profondità le onde sismiche improvvisamente acceleravano: segno che stavano attraversando un materiale diverso, più denso e rigido. Quella era la firma del mantello.
Da allora il Moho è diventato uno dei riferimenti fondamentali della geofisica, ma resta un confine "visto" solo indirettamente, attraverso le onde sismiche. Sotto gli oceani si trova a 5-10 chilometri di profondità, ma i fondali marini sono difficili e costosi da perforare. Sotto i continenti, invece, scende in media a 30-40 chilometri, e sotto le grandi catene montuose può superare i 60-70: una profondità impensabile per qualunque trivella oggi esistente.. La Valsesia fa eccezione
Ed è qui che entra in gioco un angolo di Piemonte. Chi conosce le Alpi tende a immaginare che, come in ogni catena montuosa, anche qui il Moho sia sepolto molto in profondità, sotto montagne che pesano e affondano nel mantello come un iceberg nell'acqua. In gran parte della catena è effettivamente così: sotto le Alpi occidentali la crosta si ispessisce e la Moho raggiunge anche i 50 chilometri e oltre.
Nella zona Ivrea-Verbano, però, la storia è diversa. Quando, decine di milioni di anni fa, la placca africana si scontrò con quella europea dando origine alle Alpi, un enorme frammento di crosta profonda e di mantello superiore fu spinto verso l'alto, fino a essere inclinato e portato vicino alla superficie.. Il risultato è un vero e proprio "spaccato" naturale della crosta: le rocce che normalmente si trovano a 20-30 chilometri di profondità affiorano oggi sulle nostre montagne, e le indagini geofisiche indicano che la Moho si trova qui a circa 2 chilometri sotto la superficie, contro i 30 e più della norma continentale.
In altre parole, non serve più scavare per decine di chilometri: in Valsesia la crosta profonda è già in superficie e il mantello è a portata di trivella. Non è un caso che in zona affiori la peridotite di Balmuccia, una roccia che proviene proprio dal mantello superiore ed è uno dei rari esempi al mondo visibili in superficie. Per questo l'area è considerata da decenni uno dei luoghi di riferimento per studiare l'intera sezione tra crosta e mantello.. Il progetto DIVE
Il sogno di perforare fino al mantello nasce negli anni Sessanta, con il celebre progetto americano Mohole, che puntava a bucare il fondale oceanico e fu abbandonato per difficoltà tecniche e costi. In pochissimi casi si è riusciti a scapito di sforzi enormi. Oggi la comunità scientifica internazionale ha individuato nella zona Ivrea-Verbano l'occasione migliore e l'ha messa al centro del progetto DIVE (Drilling the Ivrea-Verbano zonE).. Il pozzo di Vocca
Il percorso è stato lungo. Nel maggio 2017 un workshop dell'ICDP a Baveno concluse che quattro perforazioni tra Val Sesia e Val d'Ossola rappresentavano la strategia scientificamente più promettente. Seguirono i rilievi sul campo: nel 2020 due campagne sismiche congiunte, con GFZ Potsdam, Università di Losanna e Montanuniversität Leoben, indagarono la struttura profonda dell'area, compresa la zona di Balmuccia.
La prima fase, tra il 2022 e il 2024, ha riguardato la Val d'Ossola, con due pozzi a Ornavasso e Pieve Vergonte, profondi 579 e 910 metri. Non hanno raggiunto il mantello, ma hanno restituito campioni e dati preziosi sulla crosta continentale inferiore, mostrandone una variabilità inattesa. Ne sono nati numerosi studi, alcuni già pubblicati su riviste internazionali, altri ancora in corso.. Seconda fase: si scende in profondità
Il nuovo pozzo sorgerà nell'area di Vocca e dovrà scendere più del doppio dei pozzi ossolani, con l'obiettivo di raggiungere la passaggio tra crosta e mantello. Se l'impresa riuscirà, i ricercatori potranno finalmente analizzare la Moho direttamente: carotaggi di roccia, misure di temperatura, proprietà fisiche e fluidi.. Perché è importante toccare la Moho?
Capire com'è fatta e come funziona la zona di passaggio tra crosta e mantello aiuta a ricostruire l'evoluzione del pianeta, a comprendere come circolano i fluidi nella crosta e come si formano e si distribuiscono i giacimenti di minerali strategici, oggi sempre più importanti per la transizione energetica e tecnologica..

items.title: Smetti di pagare il cloud ogni mese: ecco i NAS UGREEN scontati per la Festa delle Offerte Prime
items.summary: Lo sai quanto spenderai in abbonamenti cloud negli anni in cui custodirai i tuoi documenti e le tue foto? Con un NAS paghi una volta sola, e dal 6 all'11 ottobre UGREEN ha in sconto sei dispositivi ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Dal 6 ottobre Amazon apre la Festa delle Offerte Prime, 48 ore di sconti riservati agli abbonati Prime, e UGREEN concentra in questi due giorni i ribassi più alti della sua promozione d'autunno sui NAS NASync : sei modelli scontati sia su Amazon sia sul sito del produttore.

Un NAS (Network Attached Storage) collega al router uno o più hard disk e li rende raggiungibili da telefoni, computer e televisori, sia sulla rete di casa sia da fuori tramite Internet.

Il secondo argomento riguarda il controllo dei dati, poiché foto, documenti e backup restano sui dischi di casa e non passano dai server di terzi.

Per tutti i NASync è presente la cifratura delle connessioni con TLS/SSL, RSA e AES , l'autenticazione a due fattori e un Security Manager che controlla il sistema in modo continuo. I NAS hanno ottenuto anche la certificazione di sicurezza ETSI EN 303 645, rilasciata da TÜV SÜD, e quella statunitense TRUSTe. Anche il riconoscimento dei volti e degli oggetti nell'app Foto gira sul NAS senza inviare le immagini a servizi esterni.

C'è poi la velocità. Dentro casa i trasferimenti dipendono dalla rete locale e non dalla linea internet in upload, che nelle connessioni domestiche resta di solito il collo di bottiglia, specialmente se non si ha una fibra seria. Su una porta a 2,5 Gb/s si arriva a un massimo teorico di 312,5 MB/s, che vuol dire copiare un video 4K da 20 GB in poco più di un minuto.

È facile anche la configurazione, che sui NAS UGREEN richiede meno di dieci minuti e un'unica app per gestire file, backup delle foto e streaming verso la TV.

La prima decisione riguarda il numero di alloggiamenti per i dischi . Con due dischi si può impostare il RAID 1, che scrive gli stessi dati su entrambi: se un disco si guasta, i file restano sull'altro, ma la capienza utile è alla fine quella di un solo disco perché il secondo serve come sicurezza. Con quattro o sei alloggiamenti si possono usare il RAID 5 e il RAID 6, che salvano su tutti i dischi anche delle informazioni di controllo; quindi se un disco si rompe (due, con il RAID 6), il NAS ricostruisce i file mancanti a partire da quelli rimasti.

Conviene pensare a quanto crescerà l'archivio nei prossimi anni, perché quando tutti gli alloggiamenti saranno occupati, per avere più spazio bisognerà sostituire i dischi con altri più capienti, uno alla volta, oppure collegare un'unità esterna. Partire con un NAS a quattro alloggiamenti e due soli dischi lascia invece margine per aggiungerne altri due in seguito.

La seconda riguarda il processore. I modelli della serie DH di UGREEN usano chip ARM di Rockchip, poco energivori e sufficienti per archivio, backup e streaming , con una versione semplificata del sistema operativo UGOS Pro e memoria non espandibile.

La serie DXP monta processori Intel, ha la versione completa di UGOS Pro, memoria espandibile e due slot M.2 per SSD da usare come cache o come spazio aggiuntivo. È quindi la strada per chi vuole affiancare all'archivio carichi più pesanti , come le macchine virtuali o un server multimediale che converte i video al volo, oppure servire molti utenti insieme.

La terza e ultima scelta è quella della rete . Una porta da 1 Gb/s basta per foto e documenti, quella da 2,5 Gb/s è utile con i video pesanti, mentre i 10 Gb/s servono a chi lavora in rete su file di grandi dimensioni e ha computer e switch in grado di sfruttarli.

Il DH2300 è pensato per chi un NAS non l'ha mai avuto e vuole soprattutto mettere al sicuro le foto di famiglia, smettendo di rincorrere lo spazio libero sul telefono. Ha due alloggiamenti: con due dischi in RAID 1 ogni file viene salvato due volte e, se uno dei dischi si guasta, l'archivio resta intatto. Si configura dall'app UGREEN con una procedura guidata e, per collegare lo smartphone, basta avvicinarlo al NAS grazie all'NFC .

Collegato al televisore del salotto tramite l'uscita HDMI 4K, riproduce film e video di casa senza bisogno di un computer . Il processore Rockchip a otto core e i 4 GB di memoria bastano per archivio, backup e streaming, con una capienza che arriva a 64 TB complessivi.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre il DH2300, da listino di 246,99 euro, scende a 189,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Quando i dispositivi da salvare diventano tanti, tra gli smartphone di tutta la famiglia, i portatili e magari il lavoro da casa, due dischi si riempiono in fretta. Il DH4300 Plus raddoppia gli alloggiamenti, fino a 128 TB, e permette di scegliere il RAID 5 o il RAID 6 , che proteggono i dati sacrificando meno spazio.

La porta di rete a 2,5 Gb/s accorcia i tempi quando si salvano video pesanti, e il processore Rockchip RK3588C con 8 GB di memoria regge più persone collegate insieme. Chi ha un po' di dimestichezza può installare applicazioni aggiuntive tramite Docker , mentre per tutti gli altri restano la configurazione guidata e l'app unica del DH2300.

Nei giorni della Festa delle Offerte Prime, e fino all'11 ottobre, il prezzo scende da 439,99 euro a 319,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP4800 Plus è il modello per chi dal NAS vuole qualcosa in più di un archivio , quindi un server multimediale che converte i video al volo, qualche macchina virtuale, i backup automatici di tutti i computer di casa o dello studio.

Il processore Intel Pentium Gold a cinque core lavora con 8 GB di memoria DDR5, espandibili fino a 64 GB, e il sistema gira su un SSD dedicato da 128 GB.

Accanto ai quattro alloggiamenti per hard disk ci sono due slot per SSD M.2 , da usare come cache per velocizzare i file aperti più spesso con una capienza massima di 144 TB.

La porta da 10 Gb/s, affiancata da una seconda a 2,5 Gb/s, serve a chi lavora su file grandi da un computer collegato via cavo, e il lettore di schede SD permette di scaricare le foto della fotocamera direttamente sul NAS.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre il prezzo scende da 729,99 euro a 549,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Con sei alloggiamenti per hard disk e due per SSD, il DXP6800 Pro si rivolge a un piccolo studio professionale o a chi custodisce un archivio video di anni perché può arrivare fino a 208 TB di spazio.

Il processore Intel Core i5 a dieci core permette a più persone di lavorare contemporaneamente sugli stessi file, anche mentre il NAS esegue i backup o converte un video.

Le due porte di rete da 10 Gb/s si possono unire fino a 20 Gb/s , e le due Thunderbolt 4 servono a collegare dischi esterni veloci, per esempio per scaricare il materiale di una giornata di riprese. L 'uscita HDMI arriva fino all'8K.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre il DXP6800 Pro è in offerta, passando dal listino di 1.209,99 euro a 899,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP2800 è per chi si accontenta di due dischi ma dal NAS vuole più di un archivio di foto. Ha gli stessi due alloggiamenti del DH2300, ma monta un processore Intel più potente e la versione completa del sistema UGOS Pro , con più applicazioni a disposizione. La memoria si può ampliare fino a 16 GB e due slot per SSD servono a velocizzare i file usati più spesso.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre si scende dal listino di 439,99 euro a 329,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP480T Plus rinuncia agli hard disk e accoglie quattro SSD M.2 NVMe , così da lavorare sui file video direttamente dalla rete senza rallentamenti. Monta lo stesso Core i5 del DXP6800 Pro, una porta da 10 Gb/s e due Thunderbolt 4.

In questo caso lo sconto vale solo il 6 e 7 ottobre: in quei due giorni il prezzo di listino di 999,99 euro passa a 749,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Con la Festa delle Offerte Prime è il momento giusto per smettere di pagare lo spazio online ogni mese e riportare a casa i propri ricordi, una volta per tutte.

Sui NAS UGREEN i prezzi della festa restano validi dal 6 fino all'11 ottobre su tutti i modelli tranne il DXP480T Plus, che sale dal prezzo scontato di 749,99 euro a 899,99 euro già dall'8 ottobre. Tutte le offerte sono sulla pagina UGREEN di Amazon e sulla pagina dedicata del sito UGREEN .

items.title: What are the US midterms? A simple guide
items.summary: US voters will head to the polls on 3 November in a ballot that could have a major impact on Donald Trump’s presidency.
items.content:
There are four weeks to go until the US midterm elections, when voters take part in a ballot that could have a major impact on the rest of Donald Trump's presidency.

On 3 November, Americans will choose members of Congress, which is made up of two parts - the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Elections take place every two years, and when they happen in the middle of the president's four-year term of office, they are called the midterms.

A key task of Congress is to create and pass federal laws - laws that apply nationwide.

The outcome of the midterms will decide which political party - Trump's Republicans or opposition Democrats - controls Congress and how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans.

The results are also seen as a measure of how happy people in the US are with the president's performance so far.

All 435 members of the House - the lower chamber of Congress - will be elected. They serve fixed terms of two years. The House is commonly where proposed laws are introduced and debated.

Meanwhile, 35 of 100 seats in the Senate, the upper chamber, will also be up for grabs. Senators serve six-year terms. Among other jobs, they approve or block proposed laws that have been received from the House.

On the same day, voters across much of the US will also choose state-level politicians. Governor contests in California, Florida, Georgia and Michigan will be among the most closely watched.

The US economy is on the minds of many voters struggling with the price of fuel, groceries, housing and healthcare.

Inflation remains above the level targeted by the US Federal Reserve, partly down to the war that the US and Israel started with Iran in February.

Democrats argue Trump's programme of trade tariffs have also pushed up prices for Americans.

Immigration is another key issue. Republicans say Trump has delivered on a major campaign pledge in 2024 by tightening the border and launching a widespread - and often controversial - crackdown on illegal immigration.

Concerns over AI have grown in urgency in recent weeks. Senior politicians from both parties have agreed on the need to regulate it - setting themselves in opposition to Trump, who has rejected the idea of laws to control development of the technology.

Congress is one of the three branches of government, alongside the presidency and the judiciary. Control of it matters for the shaping of legislation.

Both the House and Senate are currently held by the Republican Party. But its majority is a slender one. They have 218 seats in the House, which is the minimum number needed to control it, plus one independent who votes with them. In the Senate, they have 53 seats and the minimum needed for control is 51.

If opposition Democrats win back control of at least one chamber, they will gain power to bring their own laws to the floor.

Voters have tended to "punish" the party of the president in the past and vote against them.

Recent polling shows a low approval rating for the president. He began his second term as president with an approval rating of just over 50%, according to polling resource website Silver Bulletin, but in early October it was sitting at about 37%. Meanwhile 61% disapproved of him.

But not all seats in each chamber are competitive. Some are a safe bet for Republicans or Democrats.

The BBC's US partner CBS News has identified nine Senate races to watch , external , in states like Iowa and New Hampshire, and 42 House races, in states like Arizona and Ohio.

The vote is more unpredictable this year because of a battle between the two parties over the way voting districts in the House of Representatives are drawn.

Republicans tried to gain an advantage by creating more favourable electoral maps in certain states and Democrats followed suit.

If the Democrats win either the House or the Senate then Trump will find it difficult to get any laws through Congress.

So his domestic plans could be frustrated, although he has found ways to exercise power without his wider party.

Democratic control of either chamber would also mean they could use committees to investigate aspects of the Trump presidency. Corruption allegations, the new White House ballroom and ICE tactics could be subject to scrutiny.

There is also a debate within the Democratic Party about whether to impeach Trump, which means to bring charges in Congress that will form the basis for a political, not criminal, trial.

If the Republican Party stays in control of Congress, Trump will be able to keep going with his plans for the remainder of his time in office.

The president's name is not on the ballot during the midterm elections, though Trump has urged Republicans to pretend that it is by voting for him as an endorsement of his actions so far.

Whichever way the results fall, commentators are likely to use them to make arguments about how voters feel about the direction of the country under Trump's leadership.

Trump cannot run to be president a third time. After the midterms, we can expect speculation to start building about who might be his successor as the Republican presidential nominee for 2028 - and who might compete against that person for the Democrats.

items.title: Samon: Designing a Zen Garden Raking Puzzle
items.summary: Article URL: https://gwern.net/doc/design/2026-10-03-gwern-samon.html Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49972211 Points: 42 # Comments: 20
items.content:
Zen sand gardens are often intended for meditation, whether to look at or while maintaining it by raking the sand into the prescribed patterns which are formed by the tines of the rake yielding parallel lines (like ||| ). Such a chore might be tedious, but there is also a great deal of satisfaction to restoring an esthetic order from chaos, and raking sand seems like one of those things, like popping bubblewrap, which can be oddly satisfying—I recall the lifeguards at my summer camp seeming to rather enjoy the task of raking the beach in front of their office every day and not allowing any campers to do so. Puzzle-solving is also often described as being ‘meditative’ and ‘oddly satisfying’, even when it looks a lot like a tedious chore. So for those of us who do not live at a Zen temple, can we make a Zen sand garden puzzle ?

This page turns the original 2023 sketch into a full design. Where the sketch speculated (would “mirror raking” be too restrictive? could a neural net rank solutions by beauty? how should difficulty be raised?), we answer with a solver and measurements; where it left gaps (what exactly makes a garden hard, what the worlds are, how levels are generated, what the player touches), we fill them. The title is Samon (砂紋, “sand crest”), the term for the patterns themselves. 1

Pieces. A garden is a walled rectangle of white gravel—in Kyoto, typically Shirakawa-suna , weathered granite from the Kitashirakawa area ( Nabunken )—divided into square cells, with stones as obstacles. One cell on the veranda side is the gate : the gap in front of the kutsunugi-ishi , the flat stone below the veranda where one removes one’s shoes ( JAANUS ). The player is an unsui , a novice monk, and the garden is viewed, as at Ryōan-ji , from the abbot’s veranda: the bottom edge of the screen.

The rule. The novice steps off the shoe-stone, walks into the sand, puts down his rake, and walks backwards to the gate, dragging the rake over his own footprints. The garden is finished when every cell of sand has been raked exactly once, the lines are unbroken, and he is back on the shoe-stone. That is the whole rule: one stroke, every cell once, no crossing, ending at the gate.

Formally: Hamiltonian paths. Formally, the sand cells form a grid graph, and a valid raking is a Hamiltonian path of that graph which ends at the gate cell. The rake lines are the path’s shape: a cell traversed straight gets parallel grooves; a cell where the path turns gets concentric quarter-circles; the cell where the rake was set down gets the groove’s start. Every claim below about counts, pars, and difficulty comes from an exact solver for this formulation (see Methods ).

Walking in is free. The original sketch distinguished the forward walk (leaving footprints) from the backward raking, and proposed “mirror raking”—the monk retraces his walk exactly—as a possibly-too-restrictive simplification. It is not a restriction at all. Any walk in, followed by a raking that covers every cell exactly once and ends at the gate, erases every footprint, because every cell gets raked; so the walk in is irrelevant except for where it ends, and the set of finished gardens is exactly the set of Hamiltonian paths ending at the gate. Conversely, every such path is achieved by walking it in and raking it out. 2 So mirror raking loses nothing, and the interface can be the simplest possible: draw a path from the gate ; that path is the walk in; the raking is its reverse.

This matters for design because the story stays intact (the reveal is the monk raking himself out of the garden) while the player’s task is a single, legible gesture.

Too many rakings. The one-stroke rule alone is a weak constraint in open sand. For an empty garden with a corner gate, the number of valid rakings is the number of Hamiltonian paths from a corner, OEIS A145157 , which grows explosively: 824 for 5×5, 1,510,446 for 7×7, 54,986,690,944 for 9×9. (Our solver reproduces A145157 and the 5× n sequence A145156 exactly, which is a useful correctness check.) Anyone can rake an open garden: walk up and down in rows.

Parity. Stones make the rule bite, but mostly by making gardens impossible . Color the cells like a checkerboard: every step of the stroke changes color, so a stroke over n cells alternates colors, and if one color has more cells, the stroke must begin and end on it. A 5×5 garden has 13 dark and 12 light cells, so its gate must be on a dark cell; move the gate one cell along the wall and there is no raking at all. Of random 7×7 gardens with a gate somewhere on the veranda wall, 57% pass this parity test with no stones and only 31% with 6 stones.

Random stones: unsolvable or open. Past parity, stones create dead ends (a cell with one free neighbor must be where the rake is set down—at most one such cell may exist) and corridors (a cell with two free neighbors must use both). These are the classic deductions of one-stroke puzzles, and they are real, but random stone placement produces them in the wrong proportion: gardens are either unsolvable or still have thousands of rakings. In 300 random 7×7 gardens per row, none with 0–6 random stones had a unique raking:

The bare rule therefore cannot carry a game by itself: completion is trivial in open sand, and the obstacles that make it non-trivial mostly make it impossible. Two things fix this: a score that makes the slack matter, and rules that remove it. Pleasingly, both come from what makes a raked garden beautiful.

The abbot counts turns. The commonest samon are long parallel lines, interrupted where they ring a stone. A raking that zigzags looks agitated. So the game’s single esthetic metric is the number of turns : every cell where the stroke changes direction. Fewer turns is calmer. Each garden has a par , the minimum number of turns over all valid rakings, proven by a constraint solver (in a few seconds at most, for gardens up to 9×9). Any valid raking finishes the garden; a raking at par earns the abbot’s vermilion seal.

Par is a needle. Turns make the looseness useful. The distribution of turns over all valid rakings is a broad hump, and par sits in the far tail: in the empty 7×7 garden, 66 of 1,510,446 rakings (0.004%) reach par, and the median raking has more than twice as many turns. Finishing a garden is easy; finishing it calmly is a real optimization puzzle, of the kind where intuition (“make long lines; circle the stones; use the walls”) gets close and the last two turns take thought.

Histograms. This is the structure of Zachtronics optimization games, where after solving, the player’s solution is ranked against every other player’s on a few metrics ( Opus Magnum compares cycles, cost, and area). Samon shows one histogram per garden after completion: the player’s turn count against everyone’s, with par marked—a picture very like the one above, filled in by real players. Because par is proven , the seal is never a trap (no “par” that nobody can reach) and never a lie (no raking can beat it).

Par tends to look traditional. The surprise is that minimizing a single number recovers the traditional motifs. In the open and lightly-stoned gardens we inspected, par rakings were nested U-bends and spirals: long parallel lines across the garden ( sazanami ), and concentric rings around stones ( mizumon ), without either being specified. The rings appear because circling a stone is the cheapest way to use the cells next to it; the parallel lines appear because every turn costs. This is not a law, though: with crowded or awkwardly-placed stones, par rakings degenerate into meanders full of tight U-turns in open sand. Among 60 random solvable gardens (6×7–7×8, 1–3 stones), only 40% admitted any raking free of open-sand U-turns, and only 20% had a par raking that was free of them; so “par is beautiful” is a property for the level curator to select for (and we do: see Generating Gardens ), not something the rule guarantees.

Why not a neural esthetic score? The sketch proposed ranking solutions with a learned esthetic model, such as the CLIP-based predictor behind LAION-Aesthetics . For scoring the player , a hand-countable metric is better: the player can see it, count it, and deliberately optimize it, and a proven optimum exists; an opaque neural score can be none of these, and would invite adversarial raking. The learned model is better spent upstream, ranking layouts (which stone arrangements look like real gardens, which par rakings are prettiest when several tie), where opacity costs nothing.

One rule per world. The standing criticism of Zen Puzzle Garden , the closest ancestor, was monotony: “there’s still a persisting feeling that, even by the final few stages, Zen Puzzle Garden hasn’t developed one step beyond what the tutorial already demonstrated” ( Wilson 2011 ). So each world adds one rule, and each rule must earn its place by changing how the player thinks , not just the scenery. Every rule below is diegetic—a thing in the garden or a property of the rake—and every one was tested with the solver on random gardens before being kept. Here are the candidates that survived, in the order the game introduces them, and then the ones that did not.

items.title: Five reasons India's stock market is sinking even when its economy is growing
items.summary: The world's fastest growing major economy has one of the worst performing major equity markets in 2026.
items.content:
India's economy is growing at an enviable rate of over 7% despite global energy shocks, rising interest rates, tariff uncertainties and weather-related disruptions.

But the world's fastest growing major economy also has one of the worst performing major equity markets in 2026. The correction in Indian stocks has, in fact, only intensified in recent weeks.

The benchmark Sensex and Nifty indices, which represent the country's largest companies, have inched up slightly since Monday after posting losses for eight straight weeks - the longest losing streak in 25 years, according to Reuters.

Indian mom-and-pop investors who put their money into the Nifty have seen their wealth erode by about 15% this year. In comparison, they would have made 62% returns on Korea's Kospi index since January or 170% in the last two years.

On aggregate, the money foreign investors have put into Indian markets in the past decade - after subtracting what they sold or withdrew - is nearing zero. In the past two years alone, foreign institutional investors have withdrawn a staggering $40bn, according to data from Bernstein Research.

It is the large pool of domestic institutional and retail money, flowing into instruments like mutual funds, that have helped the markets avoid a sharper fall.

Domestic assets under management of mutual funds have grown from about $125bn in 2016 to some $900bn this year, with the number of Indians parking money in stocks and mutual funds more than tripling to 150 million individuals.

This makes the recent fall in the markets more worrying - since households, already struggling from a weak job market, high inflation and faltering consumption, are now seeing their equity savings take a beating too.

Here are five reasons India's booming economy isn't lifting its stock market.

Crude oil prices have hovered between $90 and $100 a barrel as the disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz enters its eighth month, far longer than analysts had expected. Moreover, there's little visibility on when normalcy will return.

"This single variable tends to influence the markets quite negatively," Hari Shyamsunder, a fund manager with Franklin Templeton Asset Management India, told the BBC. "Markets can absorb crude between $70 and $90, but when prices move above $100 a barrel, it starts putting stress on macro-economic variables such as inflation and also company earnings and margins."

India imports over 90% of its requirements - nearly half of its crude oil imports, along with a large share of its liquified petroleum gas (LPG) and liquified natural gas (LNG) shipments, come through the Strait of Hormuz.

While Delhi has diversified its energy sources, tapping Russian oil markets, US President Donald Trump recently threatened up to 100% tariffs on countries doing trade with Moscow, further complicating matters.

With oil prices rising, inflation is going up and, as a result, interest rates are on the rise globally. The effective yield on US government bonds is above 5%, or at near 25-year highs.

These are often considered risk-free investments. As a result, foreign money tends to leave riskier emerging market assets such as Indian equities and chase safer investments like US bonds when interest rates rise.

For foreign investors, the problem of muted returns has been compounded by a weaker rupee. In currency-adjusted dollar terms, they have suffered because of the fall in the Indian currency.

The Nifty has delivered just 6% annualised dollar returns over the past decade - hardly attractive, especially in comparison with several other competing markets.

The market correction over the last two years has reduced the premium that Indian stocks held over their emerging market competitors.

"Stocks are cheaper than they have been on average for the last ten years," says Shyamsunder, adding that the premium that Indian shares commanded over other emerging economies has shrunk substantially in the past few years.

However, they are still expensive relative to their earnings, especially since companies in countries such as South Korea and Taiwan have benefited from a huge boom in artificial intelligence (AI) which has pushed up their profits.

In India, AI, or the new economy broadly, is a major missing piece of its growth story.

"Many of India's large caps [big companies] represent a bygone economic era," Bernstein Research said in a note recently. "Most are not investing in the future, but consolidating their past, often expecting policy to continue shielding them from global competition."

And its smaller companies are yet to reach a scale that will attract foreign institutional funds.

While Indian companies are investing in data centres and chip fabrication, the country has not produced a global giant like OpenAI, Anthropic or even China's DeepSeek - this is where the largest share of the profits in the AI value chain lie.

Foreign investor interest will only return to India meaningfully if it can build globally competitive industries in these emerging areas, according to Bernstein.

"We are seeing early signs of this in areas such as space, defence, semiconductors, and deep-tech innovation, but most remain too small to materially influence capital allocation decisions over much of this decade."

There are many immediate factors that will influence how Indian markets behave going forward.

"Easing geopolitical tensions and relatively attractive valuations could support a revival in FPI [foreign portfolio investor] inflows," according to CareEdge, a brokerage, though trade tensions and higher energy prices remain a “challenge for corporate performance going ahead”.

To what extent corporate margins have been squeezed will become clearer as they start reporting quarterly earnings from this week.

For now, while foreign investors may have given up, Indian savers, even though increasingly more anxious, haven't slowed their monthly investment flows , external into mutual funds.

The real test will be whether this resilience survives a deeper correction in the future.

items.title: Blue Planet and Gandhi composer George Fenton dies aged 76
items.summary: The musician received five Oscar nominations, and soundtracked dozens of memorable nature films.
items.content:
Composer George Fenton, whose work included music for films such as Gandhi, Groundhog Day and The Fisher King, as well as TV shows like Planet Earth and Bergerac, has died at the age of 76.

The prolific musician received five Oscar nominations for his film scores, including those for Dangerous Liasions and Cry Freedom.

His work on the BBC TV show Blue Planet also earned awards from the Baftas, Emmy Awards and Ivor Novellos; and he also composed theme music for BBC News programmes such as Newsnight and Breakfast Time.

In a statement, Fenton's family said: "We are very sad to announce that George Fenton passed away unexpectedly today."

They continued: "He is survived by his loving wife Amanda, ex-wife Jane, children Gemma, Grace and Bridget, and grandchildren Lola, Audrey, Alfred, George, Frank and Beatrice, and a life of music."

The cause of death was not disclosed but, underlining the suddenness of his passing, Fenton had signed a new worldwide publishing deal just three weeks ago , external .

At the time, he said he was working on two new film scores and a musical.

Fenton was born George Howe in Bromley, Kent in 1949. According to a biography on his official website , external , his father was a mechanical engineer, and his mother had been a dancer before becoming a nurse during the war.

Both parents were musical - his father played drums and his mother played piano - but Fenton chose the electric guitar as his instrument at the age of seven.

That was "when music became more important than football," he later told The Express newspaper , external . "The Beatles had a huge influence on me."

He took his first lessons from a musician called Brian Rudd.

"He came into our lives as a chimney sweep, which he clearly wasn't," Fenton later recalled.

"My mother went mad at him because he filled the house with soot.

"As he left he said, 'I'm really sorry – but I tuned the boy's guitar for you.' She suggested that as compensation for the mess he could give me a lesson, which he did and then carried on doing."

Later, Fenton began to study the church organ, but rejected the offer of music college to pursue a stage career.

In 1968, he appeared in Alan Bennett's first West End play Forty Years On. Upon joining the actor's union Equity, he was forced to adopt his mother's maiden name, due to rules preventing two actors from sharing the same name.

During that production, he also understudied the musical director of the show, Carl Davis - who also became a prominent composer for film and television.

A year later, Fenton signed a record deal, and scored a top 10 hit in Sweden with a cover of The Beatles' Maxwell's Silver Hammer , external , but his career as a solo artist was short lived.

In the mid-1970s, he took a recurring role as the soldier Martin Gimbel in the ITV soap opera Emmerdale Farm.

But as time went on, he found that directors were always casting him in roles that required him to play an instrument, so he decided to make music his main focus.

Fenton got his first job as composer and musical director for a production of Twelfth Night at the Royal Shakespeare Company in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1974.

Eight years later, he was nominated for an Oscar for his score for Richard Attenborough's Gandhi , external , on which he worked with Indian composer and instrumentalist Ravi Shankar to develop themes reflecting the country's musical traditions.

It was only his fourth attempt at film music, and he was still almost entirely self-taught.

Throughout the 1980s, he wrote the soundtrack for a number of TV series, including the Bafta-winning The Jewel in the Crown, The Monocled Mutineer, and Alan Bennett's Talking Heads.

He also wrote many well-known theme tunes, including the BBC's One O'Clock News, Six O'Clock News, Nine O'Clock News, Newsnight, The Money Programme, and Radio 4's PM Programme.

For 1987's Cry Freedom - the story of South African campaigner Steve Biko, who was brutally killed by police - he worked with South African jazz musician Jonas Gwangwa, earning two Oscar nominations for best original score and song.

Almost by accident, the title track featured Fenton singing , external a list of anti-apartheid activists imprisoned or killed by the South African government.

He'd initially recorded the lyrics as a guide for Gwangwa - but the musician decided to keep some of them intact "as a gesture of brotherhood".

"Then it got nominated for an Oscar, so I then found myself singing it on live television to about a billion people, which was not what I intended at all," Fenton later told Radio 4's Desert Island Discs.

After composing the score for the BBC's Trials of Life in 1990, Fenton went on to create the music for what became known as David Attenborough's Earth Trilogy: The Blue Planet , external , Planet Earth and Frozen Planet.

Fenton's music perfectly complemented the stunning visuals of the ocean's depths and the polar ice caps, adding an emotional weight to the narrative, using the full might of the orchestra to evoke everything from wonder and awe to tension and suspense.

Following the success of the documentaries, Fenton created a show - The Blue Planet in Concert - which has been performed by leading orchestras in venues around the world.

Among his other well-known soundtracks were The Long Walk Home, You've Got Mail, Sweet Home Alabama, The Lady In The Van and Mrs Henderson Presents.

Fenton also scored more films for British director Ken Loach than any other composer.

Their 18 collaborations included Ladybird, Ladybird; I, Daniel Blake and The Wind That Shakes the Barley, which won the Palme d'Or at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival.

He also founded the Association of Professional Composers, which later merged with The Ivors Academy; and he is one of only a handful of musicians to receive the Academy's fellowship, alongside Sir Andrew Lloyd Webber, Sir Elton John, Kate Bush, Bruce Springsteen and George Michael.

In addition, Fenton was a visiting professor at the Royal College of Music and the University of Nottingham. He was made a CBE for services to music in 2023.

The composer often said that his musical career had been an accident, but nothing gave him greater joy than seeing his work come to life.

On his episode of Desert Island Discs, Fenton chose one of his own compositions - Reunion, from the soundtrack to the movie Accidental Hero - as it reminded him of watching pianist John Lowe play the melody in the studio.

"If I was sitting on a desert island and thinking about what a good time I'd had writing music, which I have, I want just one thing to remind me about the best part - which is the fact that you write something and then you're so surprised and thrilled at the way it's played," he told Sue Lawley.

items.title: Example.com just launched the biggest redesign in decades
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.debugbear.com/blog/example-dot-com-redesign-history Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49971921 Points: 215 # Comments: 137
items.content:
example.com is a reserved domain name set aside by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) for documentation purposes. It has been available as an example URL for developers and writers since the late nineties.

While the overall messaging of the page has been consistent over time, the visual appearance has received several major overhauls.

In this article, we take a look at the recent changes as well as the evolution of example.com over the last 20+ years.

Until 28 September 2026, example.com was a static English-language page. The redesign introduces multi-language support using JavaScript, showing the content in a new language every 5 seconds.

Example.com shows an explanation of the site's purpose in English, Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian and Spanish. This is the English-language message:

This domain is for use in documentation examples without needing permission. This is not a service, avoid relying on it for testing and monitoring purposes.

Along with introducing multi-language support, the JavaScript code also inserts an SVG book icon.

The new site doesn't just replace the content when showing the next language. Instead, there's a gradual opacity transition.

The opacity animation itself just uses transition: opacity .4s; . But how is the character-by-character transition implemented?

Each character is wrapped in its own span element, and each span gets a slightly larger CSS transition-delay than the one before it. That means each character's opacity animation happens at a slightly different time.

IANA provided the following statement explaining the reasoning behind the recent changes:

The changes we make to the site from time-to-time are usually informed by a desire to either reduce the overall bandwidth demands of serving the site, or improve its utility. At its heart it is a placeholder for a site no-one should be accessing, but we have historically showed a message there to inform visitors about why the domain is registered and how they may use it.

As it tends to be heavily trafficked, the overall bandwidth is a key consideration, and to that end one of the changes we made this week was to split the page content into a more basic page, augmented by a separate Javascript file with additional content beyond that. Since most of the traffic to the site is automated it tends not to fetch the Javascript file, reducing overall data requirements.

The fundamental purpose of the domain is for use in documentation, such as illustrative examples you may find in instructions. We know that people may, for example, cut-and-paste a sample configuration file and forget to customize entries that contain an example domain, and we expect we get some incidental traffic from that. However, the domain isn't intended to be a general purpose endpoint for things like availability testing so we do not encourage that kind of usage. There is no requirement there is a HTTP service present on the host in order to fulfill its purpose, we just operate it as a courtesy.

According to Wikipedia , the example.com website launched on January 1, 1999. The earliest version available to view in the Wayback Machine is from January 20, 2002.

The earliest version of the website only featured a list of domain names reserved by the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) and IANA.

In the .com, .net, and .org top-level domains (TLDs), various domain names are reserved. These names are reserved from initial registration, but to the extent they are already registered the existing registrant may renew them.

Structurally, the HTML used a table layout, with the ICANN logo positioned in the top left corner of the page.

The server headers show that the site used Apache 1.3.22 at this point.

The first version of the example.com wording we recognize today came 67 days after the first available screenshot:

You have reached this web page by typing "example.com", "example.net", or "example.org" into your web browser.

These domain names are reserved for use in documentation and are not available for registration.

In February 2003, the content was amended to include a link to RFC 2606 , the official document for reserved top-level and second-level domains, so visitors could find more information on the website's purpose.

There was also a small technical change around this time: the server was upgraded to Apache 1.3.27 on Red Hat Linux.

The website then went unchanged for seven years. On July 30, 2010, a slight change was made: example.edu was now pointed to the landing page, alongside the three previous domains.

From January 2011, example.com didn't serve its own page. Instead, it redirected visitors to a page on IANA's website.

That changed on July 29, 2013, when the redirect was removed and example.com began serving its own page from the EdgeCast Content Delivery Network (CDN) instead of Apache, alongside a major redesign of the landing page. The new design used a rounded card with an reading 'Example Domain' and a new description of the website's purpose.

The viewable domain list was now gone, with a link to IANA's website for more information.

A new update came six years after the biggest change in the website's history. The layout remained the same, but the font stack was modernized to include more fallback fonts for devices such as Macs, iPhones, and Windows PCs.

The copy was tweaked slightly, with 'is for use in illustrative examples' replacing 'established to be used' and 'in literature' replacing 'in examples'.

Almost twelve years after the switch from Apache to the EdgeCast CDN, another infrastructure change took place: the Server header disappeared entirely. The response headers alone don't reveal which platform was serving the page at this point.

A change of provider around this time isn't surprising. EdgeCast had been acquired from Yahoo by Limelight Networks in 2022 and rebranded as Edgio. Edgio then filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in late 2024, with Akamai acquiring select Edgio customer contracts.

Later in 2025, the page was redesigned. The card design was dropped, and the HTML was minified. The copy was changed to a more direct message, again linking to IANA's website, with the link text changed from 'More information...' to 'Learn more'.

Less than a year after the previous switch, the infrastructure changed again: the site now serves from Cloudflare , as indicated by the cloudflare server header and CF-RAY header in the response. Whatever platform served the page after the January 2025 change, it has now been replaced with a Cloudflare-fronted setup.

The next update, on June 9, 2026, brought no visual changes. The only HTML changes on the page itself were a favicon tag being added and the tags being closed. The page now includes an empty favicon:

This avoids a lot of unnecessary requests, as otherwise browsers look for a favicon at /favicon.ico .

Example.com first introduced an "Avoid use in operations" message in 2025.

For developers, it's tempting to use example.com to check if the network is working or test HTTP requests. The example server likely receives a lot of traffic through this.

However, as the page now clarifies, it's not a service you can rely on. When we look at our uptime monitoring data, we can see that every now and then the example.com server doesn't respond correctly.

Using infrastructure that your organization controls can be more reliable.

Looking at the visual timeline, we can see that changes to example.com happen sporadically. Sometimes a couple of small tweaks happen in back-to-back months. Other times the website remains untouched for periods of up to seven years.

We have been monitoring the page for several years in our public demo project. The Chrome UX Report (CrUX) data shows how page speed has changed over time.

items.title: ChatGPT is adding real cartoonists' signatures to fake New Yorker cartoons
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.niemanlab.org/2026/10/chatgpt-is-adding-real-cartoonists-signatures-to-fake-new-yorker-cartoons/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49971846 Points: 425 # Comments: 308
items.content:
At the pearly gates, Dolly Parton, in a sparkling gown, stands arm in arm with Tim Curry, dressed as Dr. Frank-N-Furter. “I knew I chose the right plus one,” Parton says to God, who is standing at heaven’s reception desk.

That’s the premise of a cartoon that went viral on Twitter in the days after the legendary entertainers’ deaths in late August. One tweet of the cartoon received 25,000 likes, while other versions of the image circulated on Facebook , Instagram , and Bluesky .

In the bottom right corner of the cartoon is the pen name “BLOPER,” the signature of New Yorker cartoonist Brendan Loper . But Loper didn’t draw the cartoon, or sign it. It was generated by ChatGPT and first posted to Facebook by a Dolly Parton fan. In the comments section of her post, she wrote she had simply asked ChatGPT to make “a New Yorker-style cartoon.”

“I had people writing to me about this cartoon, asking if it was mine,” Loper told me. First came a text from his twin brother, whose friend had seen the AI-generated image. Emails and DMs on social media from strangers followed. “It was very surreal,” he said.

A cartoon generated by ChatGPT and signed with Brendan Loper’s signature that was posted to Twitter on August 26, 2026 .

This wasn’t the first time ChatGPT had reproduced Loper’s signature. In May, a stranger reached out over Instagram to warn Loper that his pen name had appeared in an image output by the chatbot. Over the summer, Loper found additional examples in a Reddit forum about ChatGPT, where users had been posting similar New Yorker-style cartoons they had generated.

Loper already knew his work was “out there, getting harvested for all of this [AI] training,” he said. But an image generator faking his signature felt more personal. “I’m not a territorial person, but my name is my name. It felt very much like a violation of my personhood.”

RELATED ARTICLE “I don’t want to outsource my brain”: How political cartoonists are bringing AI into their work Andrew Deck June 2, 2025 These days, cartoon signatures are more than a byline. In an era where cartoons are regularly stripped from their original context and circulated on blogs and social media without proper licensing, they can also act as a watermark that ties an illustration to its original creator.

“The signature for me is the certificate of authenticity. I only put it on work that I’m putting on the internet that I feel needs to be recognized as from my hand,” Loper told me. “If I put my name on it, it’s official, it’s mine. It really is a brand. It’s the mark that I made.”

Loper isn’t the only New Yorker cartoonist whose signature has been reproduced by ChatGPT. In the same online forums are dozens of images with those of other prominent contributors, including Harry Bliss , Emily Flake , Joe Dator , Pat Byrnes , Peter Vey , and Jason Adam Katzenstein . In my own tests, ChatGPT output cartoons with signatures of some of the magazine’s most established cartoonists, past and present, including George Booth , Liza Donnelly , Ellis Rosen , and Saul Steinberg . In all, I documented more than 15 New Yorker cartoonists whose signatures have been used by OpenAI’s image generator without permission or compensation.

“We believe the future of creativity is one that is fundamentally human, and our focus is on building tools that empower human creativity and creators,” said a spokesperson for OpenAI in a statement. “We very much appreciate the community flagging bugs and unintended behavior by our models, so we can address them.”

After I notified OpenAI of the issue, ChatGPT began to output a new message when I asked it to generate New Yorker-style cartoons: “This prompt may violate our guardrails concerning similarity to third-party content.” Still, as of the publication of this story, it continues to sign some of the generic cartoons it generates with the names of real New Yorker cartoonists.

In my tests, ChatGPT regularly generated cartoons with the hallmarks of the 101-year-old magazine’s house style: a black-and-white, single-panel illustration with a sparse background, clean linework, and a sardonic caption — or at least, an approximation of one. Some of ChatGPT’s punch lines don’t make sense.

Not every image came with a signature, and some included pen names that were gibberish. But the signatures that did appear were regularly those of real contributors to the magazine, including older cartoonists, like Warren Miller , who published in the 1960s.

“I can see the DNA of my work in there, but it still doesn’t look like something I drew,” said Emily Flake, who’s been a New Yorker contributor since 2008. Several ChatGPT-generated cartoons posted online are signed with her pen name, “e. flake.” “It’s kind of like seeing a distant cousin.”

The character stances and shading contained echoes of Flake’s visual identity, but she said overall they looked more like amalgamations of several different cartoonists’ illustration styles. Each signature, though, was undeniably hers. “It’s like somebody attributed a quote to me that I didn’t say.”

Top: A cartoon generated by ChatGPT and signed with Emily Flake’s signature that was posted to a Reddit forum in June. Bottom: A real Emily Flake cartoon published in The New Yorker on August 20, 2026 and licensed via The Cartoon Bank .

In 2024, Condé Nast, The New Yorker’s parent company, signed a multi-year licensing deal with OpenAI allowing it to use much of the publisher’s content in its products. The terms of the deal aren’t public, but a spokesperson for The New Yorker told me Condé Nast has never granted an LLM developer permission to train models on its cartoons. Some ChatGPT creations reproduced The New Yorker’s logo alongside cartoons; that is also not allowed in any LLM deals, the spokesperson said.

RELATED ARTICLE Hundreds of thousands of videos from news publishers like The New York Times and Vox were used to train AI models Andrew Deck October 30, 2025 OpenAI declined to answer my questions about how its models might have ingested signatures from The New Yorker’s archives during the training process.

Even if Condé Nast did want to license cartoons to OpenAI, The New Yorker’s standard cartoonist contract leaves little room for it. The magazine’s two cartoon editors work with a roster of freelancers who submit their work on spec and only get paid if a cartoon is selected for publication. I reviewed several templatized contracts for New Yorker contributing cartoonists, none of which permit licensing for AI training purposes. While The New Yorker has the right to publish commissioned cartoons first, it is not a “work for hire” arrangement and the cartoonist retains ownership of their copyright.

So how did OpenAI’s models learn those signatures? It’s possible they were scraped from the internet. Court documents released last month in the ongoing New York Times v. OpenAI lawsuit reveal the extent to which OpenAI knowingly circumvented publishers’ paywalls while developing ChatGPT. Unredacted Microsoft memos described ChatGPT as a “product that destroys its supply chain” and the data scraped to train its underlying LLMs as “the largest theft of labor in human history.”

In another memo, Jack Clark, then the policy director of OpenAI, wrote, “[O]ur work on AI and Creativity is going to increasingly lead to us creating systems that substitute for the labor of the people that define the ‘culture’ of society.” (Clark went on to co-found Anthropic.)

RELATED ARTICLE “An astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions”: Court records show what Microsoft and OpenAI actually thought about AI training Sarah Scire September 18, 2026 Many of the cartoonists I spoke to for this story echoed Clark’s sentiment.

“It’s an uncanny simulacrum of an impression of a joke,” said Jason Adam Katzenstein , who has been publishing cartoons in The New Yorker since 2014. “But it’s not the point for it to actually be funny or good. The point is that it’s trying to deal a death blow to labor. It’s trying to render individual cartoonists obsolete because we cost money and take time.”

Katzenstein was part of the class action lawsuit filed against Anthropic in 2024 by members of the Authors Guild, the largest professional organization for published writers in the United States. Katzenstein’s cartoons had been used in an anthology published by Harper Collins, which was pirated and used by Anthropic to train its Claude models .

Last year, a judge ruled that training Claude on the authors’ work was fair use, but that Anthropic’s decision to download and maintain copies of the pirated books was a form of mass copyright infringement. In July, a federal court approved a settlement in the case , granting a $1.5 billion payout to authors and publishers — the largest in the history of U.S. copyright law.

Katzenstein considers the reproduction of his signature by ChatGPT to be more than just a violation of intellectual property; to him, it’s closer to false impersonation. “[ChatGPT] is attaching my name to work that I do not endorse or like. It’s slop, and unlike the other slop that I’ve encountered, this is slop that’s pretending to be me.”

items.title: Guerra Ucraina - Russia, le news. Massiccio attacco ucraino con 650 droni su Mosca: 2 morti
items.summary: Dopo l’allarme degli 007 tedeschi, un piano Nato per gestire un'eventuale intrusione russa
items.content:
Nuovo allarme degli 007 tedeschi, l'Estonia sposta le truppe. Per l'intelligence di Berlino si rischia la guerra con Mosca. La prossima settimana la Nato presenterà una strategia per gestire un'eventuale intrusione. Kiev schiera torrette robotiche dotate di IA per abbattere i nuovi droni russi.

L'ex capo del servizio di intelligence tedesco arrestato con l'accusa di spionaggio

Drone ucraino contro un autobus nella regione di Zaporizhzhia controllata dalla Russia: tre morti

Un attacco deliberato di un drone ucraino contro un autobus in una parte della regione di Zaporizhzhia, nel sud-est dell'Ucraina, controllata dalla Russia, ha causato martedì la morte di tre persone, ha dichiarato Yevgeny Balitsky, governatore insediato dalla Russia. Balitsky ha affermato in un messaggio su Telegram che tra le vittime c'è anche l'autista dell'autobus e che altre tre persone sono rimaste ferite. Reuters non ha potuto verificare in modo indipendente la sua dichiarazione e non c'è stato un commento immediato da parte dell'Ucraina.

L'ex capo del servizio di intelligence tedesco arrestato con l'accusa di spionaggio

L'ex capo del servizio di intelligence tedesco Bnd August Hanning è stato arrestato con l'accusa di spionaggio. A scriverlo sono la Bild e la Dpa. Hanning è stato a capo del Servizio federale di informazione dal 1998 al 2005. Le accuse contestate, scrive la Bild, sono violazione del segreto di Stato, alto tradimento e spionaggio per conto di una potenza straniera. Hanning avrebbe acquistato informazioni riservate - in cambio di denaro - da un ex collaboratore dello staff direttivo del Bnd. Lo scopo, secondo le stesse fonti, sarebbe stato quello di rivendere tali informazioni "nell'ambito della sua attività di consulenza". Il Procuratore federale ha avviato le indagini a carico di entrambi gli indagati. Gli investigatori dell'Ufficio federale di polizia criminale (Bka), scrive la Bild, hanno arrestato Hanning nelle prime ore del mattino presso la sua abitazione a Nordwalde, vicino a Münster. Contemporaneamente, in Baviera, gli agenti hanno arrestato un altro ex funzionario di alto livello del Bnd, indicato con il nome e l'iniziale del cognome, Manfred D., che in passato aveva ricoperto il ruolo di capo ufficio di Hanning e che ha lavorato per il Bnd fino alla primavera del 2026.

Kiev: “I russi colpiscono centro di Kryvyi Rih e area ospedale”

I russi hanno attaccato il territorio di un ospedale nel centro di Kryvyi Rih, ferendo un uomo e una donna. Un dipendente dell'ospedale è in gravi condizioni. Lo afferma le autorità regionali, citate da Ukrainska Pravada. I russi hanno attaccato il centro della città, dove è nato il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky, con due missili.

Mosca: “La scorsa notte colpiti centri logistici e porti in Ucraina”

Secondo quanto riferito dal ministero della Difesa di Mosca, "la scorsa notte le forze armate russe hanno condotto ulteriori attacchi con droni contro centri logistici, infrastrutture di trasporto e portuali in Ucraina, nonché navi impiegate a supporto dell'esercito ucraino". "Gli attacchi nella regione di Odessa hanno danneggiato un deposito di missili e artiglieria a Illichivk, una nave da carico nel porto di Chornomorsk, che trasportava merci a duplice uso destinate alle forze armate ucraine, infrastrutture di ormeggio utilizzate per lo scarico e lo stoccaggio di materiale militare nel porto di Izmail", si legge sul canale Telegram del ministero russo.

Due navi commerciali sono state colpite da droni nella zona economica esclusiva della Bulgaria nel Mar Nero. Lo ha reso noto il governo di Sofia, citando il soccorso marittimo bulgaro e convocando una riunione d'urgenza. Una delle navi è affondata e il suo equipaggio è disperso, secondo Roumen Nikolov, direttore del Centro di coordinamento delle operazioni di salvataggio marittimo di Varna, citato dalla radio pubblica Bnr.

Russia: “Sale a 2 morti il bilancio del maxi attacco droni ucraini su regione Mosca”

Il bilancio delle vittime dell'attacco con droni nella regione di Mosca è salito a due, con altri nove feriti: lo ha dichiarato il governatore Andrey Vorobyov citato dalla Tass. "Il bilancio delle vittime di uno dei più gravi attacchi con droni è salito a due dopo che i soccorritori hanno rinvenuto il corpo di un uomo di 71 anni sotto le macerie di un'abitazione privata a Barybino (comune di Domodedovo). Una donna che si trovava all'interno dell'abitazione è rimasta ferita", ha scritto sul suo canale Telegram. Vorobyov ha inoltre confermato che un uomo di 20 anni è rimasto ucciso nel villaggio di Radumlya, nel comune di Solnechnogorsk. Il governatore ha aggiunto che nell'attacco sono rimaste ferite nove persone.

Nella notte Mosca è stata bersaglio di un attacco di eccezionale portata che ha coinvolto 650 droni, causando almeno una vittima alla periferia della capitale russa, secondo quanto riferito dalle autorità locali. "La maggior parte di questi velivoli è stata abbattuta dalla difesa antiaerea" - inclusi 105 intercettati mentre si avvicinavano alla capitale - ha precisato il sindaco di Mosca, Sergej Sobjanin. Secondo i calcoli dell'agenzia di stampa statale Tass, si tratta del secondo attacco più massiccio contro Mosca - situata a centinaia di chilometri dal confine ucraino - registrato negli ultimi mesi, un periodo caratterizzato da un'intensificazione degli attacchi reciproci tra Ucraina e Russia. L'attacco ha provocato la morte di un giovane di 20 anni in un villaggio alla periferia di Mosca, ha riferito il governatore regionale Andrej Vorob'ëv, segnalando inoltre danni alle abitazioni in diverse località.

Il sistema di difesa aerea di Mosca ha respinto un attacco di 93 droni diretti verso la Capitale russa. Lo ha riferito il sindaco, Sergei Sobyanin, citato dai media locali.

Gli attacchi russi nel weekend e fino a ieri mattina hanno provocato vittime civili e danneggiato infrastrutture in numerose regioni, soprattutto Kharkiv e Sumy, ma anche Kiev, Donetsk, Kherson, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, Chernihiv, Mykolaiv e Odessa. Lo riferisce il portavoce dell'Onu Farhan Haq. A Kiev, ha aggiunto, è stato danneggiato il Ponte Nord, con ripercussioni sul trasporto pubblico. A Odessa, sempre secondo l'Onu, un attacco contro una nave civile ha ucciso un membro dell'equipaggio e ferito tre persone. "A settembre quasi 24 mila persone, tra cui oltre 1.800 bambini, sono state evacuate dal fronte nel Donetsk. Anche gli operatori umanitari restano nel mirino: tra luglio e agosto tre sono stati uccisi e 18 feriti", ha detto Haq.

items.title: Friendship ended with Deno, now Node is my best friend
items.summary: Article URL: https://dbushell.com/2026/10/03/deno-to-node/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49971719 Points: 161 # Comments: 88
items.content:
I’ve been using Node heavily this month on a SvelteKit client project. When did Node get so good‽ Deno has been my go-to runtime for so long I forgot how to Node. Now I’m back, I find all the ECMAScript † sugar is supported and the old annoying APIs have been replaced or modernised. Most importantly, I never have to see require() .

† Doesn’t seem like that Oracle trademark dispute will see a positive end :(

The official Node docs recommend piping an internet script straight to bash (we never learn) to install NVM to manage Node & NPM. My (ancient) experience with NVM and NPM hasn’t been stellar. I heard Fast Node Manager (FNM) was better to switch Node versions. Obviously I roll bleeding-edge but I have client projects that demand stability.

I opted for PNPM too to avoid getting immediately pwned. (The “M” in NPM stands for “malware.”) Some scripts I use have hard-coded binary names ‡ , so I added two aliases:

‡ Edit: I might be confusing the time I symlinked various binaries. The aliases do help when copying steps from install guides that assume NPM is installed.

PNPM also blocks post-install scripts. Does NPM still yolo those?

I added additional settings to pnpm-workspace.yaml to delay malware updates.

At first I tried setting the minimum release age to “one month” because it takes Microsoft at least that long to remove reported malware. This caused dependency issues where PNPM struggled to match suitable versions. I settled for “one day”; long enough to allow some other sucker to beta test the next Shai‑Hulud.

Node can now run TypeScript without throwing a tantrum like a baby if the stars don’t align. That said, one does not simply publish TypeScript packages to NPM.

Why? Just strip the types bro, I know you can! Let me sign a deal with the devil!

To discourage package authors from publishing packages written in TypeScript, Node.js refuses to handle TypeScript files inside folders under a node_modules path.

This restriction is philosophical rather than technical. I get it though. TypeScript is a Microsoft product. Opening that floodgate would pollute the entire ecosystem. Nobody wants more Microsoft. I’d love to see light “native types” in ECMAScript. There are type annotation proposals . I suspect I’ll be retired before those bear fruit.

No TypeScript packages mean I need to find the latest churnware slop to bundle my stuff. Tsdown did the trick, with only two additional dotfiles. Not thrilled about that (every dotfile represents a mistake). I suppose I break even after deleting deno.json etc.

Speaking of Microsoft lock-in, because they wrecked GitHub I’m self-hosting my own Forgejo instance . NPM limitations mean my packages have lost “provenance”. I had to configure the PNPM trust policy to allow my own stuff. Fun times!

My final test for Node was converting my static site generator from Deno. Not many Node versions ago this would have required a major refactor. Today with Node v26.10.0 I found surprisingly little work to do.

The only required changes were to replace Deno’s file system API with node:fs — which is vastly improved from what I remember (literally ~10 years ago). Aside from that, I had to replace Deno.serve with Hono’s node adapter (a wrapper around node:http ).

After this minimum-viable migration I was shocked to see 15% faster builds . My codebase still favours idiomatic Deno. I bet I’m leaving performance on the table by not using other built-in Node APIs. That’s something to explore later. The only further change I made was to replace Deno’s @std/path with node:path which is a straight import swap.

So if I were to TL;DR in the middle: Node got a glow-up, wow!

You’ve probably known this for a while. I kept using Deno out of habit and familiarity. And I haven’t exactly been enthused to write server-side JavaScript recently.

I’m burying this part because it’s flogging a dead horse. Ultimately, Deno failed when they allowed the Silicon Valley Circus to define “success”. Deno went from an innovative modern JavaScript runtime to a boring start-up with uncompelling products . Half the employees were laid off and what’s left are tweeting AI fantasies and vibe-coding Temu Cloudflare.

There is no reason to use the Deno runtime today. Deno Land Inc. stopped innovating that years ago. Node has slowly but surely caught up, even surpassing Deno in places.

Basically stuff that made it borderline unusable on top of my other criticism. JSR support were very quick to delete my account on request. I don’t like leaving dead profiles around the internet. None of my packages are visible but old versions remain installable.
